subject: CloudBridge reseller addendum — execution path, evidence checklist, and signoff
messages:
From: Sujata Kaur <sk@cloudbridge.com>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@cloudbridge.com
Date: Thu, 24 Jun 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Reseller addendum redlines and evidence request

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for sending over the draft reseller addendum. Our legal and finance teams reviewed and uploaded redlines (attached PDF) — the two items holding us up are: (1) the invoicing owner for marketplace transactions (CloudBridge requests pass-through invoicing to the seller unless Redwood can provide an invoice-ownership map), and (2) evidence scope for reseller revenue attestation (SOC2 extract + invoice traceability).

Can you confirm who at Redwood will own invoice issuance and what evidence we can reasonably provide for the first 12 months? Also, we have an internal procurement cutover date of 2026-07-12 and would like to get an execution plan (DocuSign preferred) by next week.

Attached: CloudBridge_Reseller_Addendum_v3_redlines.pdf

Best,
Sujata Kaur
Sr. Procurement Manager
CloudBridge

---
From: karthik.iyer@redwood.com <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sujata Kaur <sk@cloudbridge.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 24 Jun 2026 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Reseller addendum redlines and evidence request

Sujata — thanks for the clear callouts. Looping in legal (Marissa) and billing/ops (Ben + Laura) to confirm owners and evidence scope. High level responses:

- Invoice ownership: for marketplace listings we typically default to seller-issued invoices, but Redwood can operate as a billing intermediary if required by the partner onboarding (this impacts tax flow and settlement timing). We need to confirm which path CloudBridge requires for the first 12 months.
- Evidence: we can provide SOC2 report excerpts and transaction-level invoice trails; we will confirm retention windows with Ben.

Marissa — can you review the attached redlines and flag any legal blockers on liability/indemnity/insurance carveouts? Ben/Laura — can you confirm operational feasibility for invoice ownership switch and whether we can produce the Audit_Evidence_List as a deliverable in the SOW?

If it's helpful, I can propose an execution checklist and a tentative DocuSign envelope by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks,
Karthik
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference

---
From: marissa.cole@redwood.com <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, Sujata Kaur <sk@cloudbridge.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Reseller addendum redlines and evidence request — legal summary

Karthik / Sujata — I reviewed the CloudBridge redlines (see attached PDF). Summary of legal position and recommended path: 

1) Invoice ownership: Redwood is open to a temporary seller-invoice model (CloudBridge issues invoices to end customers) but needs explicit language in the addendum that clarifies settlement timing, fee waterfall, and audit rights. If CloudBridge prefers Redwood-issued invoices, we need a pass-through indemnity clause for tax withholdings and a 60-day holdback for disputed settlements.

2) Liability & indemnity: CloudBridge's redline broadens reseller liability (Section 6). We can accept narrowed liability for third-party claims tied to reseller misconfigurations, but cannot accept unlimited consequential damages. Proposed compromise included in the attached redline: mutual cap tied to 12 months of paid fees.

3) Evidence & audit: we can commit to providing SOC2 excerpts, per-tenant invoice trails, and a CSV export of transactions for the requested 12-month window. However, per-data-residency rules we may need to route some logs through our EU region for EU-based end-customers — ops to confirm.

Next steps (recommended):
- Ops (Ben/Laura) confirm the invoice-owner operational model and any timing impacts.
- Marissa to prepare a short negotiating memo for CloudBridge (1 page) outlining the liability/evidence compromises.
- Karthik to share the desired execution timeline; if DocuSign is agreed, Legal will prep the clean copy for signature after commercial sign-off.

Attachments: CloudBridge_Reseller_Addendum_v3_redlines.pdf

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

---
From: ben.carter@redwood.com <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, Sujata Kaur <sk@cloudbridge.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2026 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Reseller addendum redlines and evidence request — ops feasibility and runbook

Quick ops note on feasibility and execution path: 

- Invoice ownership: We can support seller-issued invoices (CloudBridge) without platform changes — that is the low-friction path. If CloudBridge wants Redwood-issued invoices, we will need to flip settlement configs in our marketplace connector and add ~2 weeks to onboarding (tax registration + EDI mapping).
- Audit evidence: attaching a draft Audit_Evidence_List_CloudBridge.xlsx that maps the artifact -> owner -> extraction method. We can produce the CSV export for month-end transactions and SOC2 excerpts, but per-tenant log extracts will take 3 business days to compile on request.
- DocuSign: if we have commercial sign-off by EOD Monday (06/28), I can stand up the DocuSign envelope and route to the CloudBridge signatories. Proposed sign-off checklist: Commercial approval -> Legal clean copy -> Ops extraction SLA confirmation -> DocuSign send.

Attachment: Audit_Evidence_List_CloudBridge.xlsx

Ben Carter
Director, Marketplace Operations
Redwood Inference

---
From: Matt Ellis <matt.ellis@cloudbridge.com>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Cc: Sujata Kaur <sk@cloudbridge.com>, marissa.cole@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2026 15:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Reseller addendum redlines and evidence request — clarifications

Thanks everyone — helpful summary. Two quick clarifications from our side before we lock the DocuSign flow: 

1) Seller-issued invoices: CloudBridge is willing to act as seller for the first 12 months but needs the settlement waterfall and reporting cadence explicitly called out (monthly reconciliations + 45-day payable terms).
2) Liability cap: the mutual 12-month paid-fees cap is acceptable, but CloudBridge asks for clearer carveouts for IP claims tied to third-party integrations.

Assuming we get the 1-page negotiating memo from Marissa today and Ben confirms the CSV extract cadence, CloudBridge will be ready to sign next week. I'll upload our internal PO and signatory matrix to your DocuSign once you send the clean copy.

Matt Ellis
Head of Partnerships (Commercial)
CloudBridge
